copy.text: Dim bars are covered. Their earlier exposure stays put.
A shortfall can take more light. Extra light cannot be removed by another exposure; Undo changes the experiment.
These are the gaps in the light already added, not the gaps between the targets. Local light can change their order.
This adds each remaining mask exposure in order. Extra local light stays extra; Undo reverses the whole press.
Seconds compare an addition. Stops compare a proportion of the target. These are light-time differences, not paper-density differences.
Add only what this chosen band lacks against its target. This does not move a mask or remove extra light.
Each checked band receives only what its own target still needs. Extra light is left alone; unchecked bands and the successive mask stay put. Undo reverses the whole press.
Change only the checked bands’ accumulated light. This is a new timing experiment, not taking light back from a real print. Undo reverses the whole press.
Checked becomes unchecked, and unchecked becomes checked. No light is added until you press an exposure button.
Move the choices, not the light. Checks wrap from one end to the other; no exposure or Undo step is added.
Checked bands receive the selected extra-light amount. The successive left-to-right mask stays where it was.
Multiply every band’s accumulated light by the same factor. The covered bands stay covered. This is a new timing experiment, not taking light back from a real print.
Scale every live band by the factor needed to match the chosen kept band. Both anchor exposures must be above zero. Masks and the kept strip stay put.
Positive differences mean more light now; negative differences mean less. This compares exposure, not print darkness.
Return only the kept light amounts. The current spacing stays selected, and the mask sequence begins again. Undo brings back the interrupted strip.

cases.title: Five bands of light — Separate checked-band experiments from whole-strip scaling
cases.goal: Choosing a band and adding light stays direct. A checked mask and a whole-strip multiplier are visibly different optional experiments, each with its own controls and help.
cases.steps: Within #strip-local-group after the one-band actions/help add two closed sibling details #strip-mask-tools and #strip-scale-tools. Mask gets #strip-custom-mask plus every existing mask action/helper through #strip-mask-help, including712 left/right and713 half/double; keep #strip-mask-scaling-help as its original inner details. Scale gets label for strip-factor, #strip-factor, #strip-scale, #strip-match-kept-band and their two help paragraphs. Keep #strip-band, #strip-dose, #strip-band-target and one-band burn/dodge/finish/help outside both. Leave successive-mask build/history and memory sections unchanged. HTML shortcode and scoped inline style only; static/darkroom-strip.js behavior is out of scope.
cases.message: checked-band experiments and whole-strip scaling keep separate doors and unchanged light history

cases.title: Five bands of light — Let the current strip lead its kept comparison
cases.goal: A current exposure plan can be read and changed without passing through its saved comparison. Saving and returning light remain one optional experiment, not a second working strip.
cases.steps: Wrap intact #strip-memory-group in closed details #strip-memory-drawer in its existing position after #strip-local-group. Preserve the group id/heading, all kept exposures/readers/help and all three controls, with existing hidden rules. Do not move #strip-undo or #strip-redo into memory; both remain in the build group. The kept strip can be visible only when its own hidden state and the drawer both permit it. No JS/state/history change. HTML shortcode and scoped inline styles only.
cases.message: current exposures lead one optional kept-strip drawer while Undo stays with the working strip
